title: Florida AI Laws

reading.body:
Florida's only AI-related law is a resolution recognizing the Tampa Bay area as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region, not a rule that binds anyone.

The measure, S1816, passed on 2026-03-12. It names CyberBay, acknowledges the state's cybersecurity preparedness, and affirms public-private collaboration. It creates no obligation, sets no effective date for compliance, and applies to no one in particular. A reader looking for what Florida requires of AI developers or deployers will not find it here.

That distinction matters for AI because state law is one of the few levers that can shape where data centers get built and how they are powered. A recognition of an innovation region is a signal of intent, and signals can precede siting decisions, utility negotiations, and incentive packages. But this text commits nothing. It does not direct funding, land, or grid capacity to the region.

The data covers one law and nothing else. It does not show pending bills, executive orders, or local ordinances, and it does not show whether CyberBay has received any state support since passage. One enacted law is a thin basis for judging Florida's posture, and the count should be read as a floor rather than a summary.

Enacted AI laws in Florida

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1816: CyberBay passed 2026-03-12

    The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Florida. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
